_about: Licences recorded by hand for packages whose metadata does not state one
that the scanners can read. 'expect' is text that must appear in the
licence file the package ships: if a new release changes its licence
file, the check fails and the entry has to be reviewed again.

colorama.expect: Neither the name of the copyright holders
colorama.reason: Windows builds only (click needs it there). Its metadata has only the classifier "BSD License"; its LICENSE.txt is the BSD 3-Clause licence.

packaging.expect: under the terms of *either* of the licenses
packaging.reason: Dual-licensed (LICENSE.APACHE or LICENSE.BSD). The copy vendored inside setuptools declares only the classifier "BSD License", which does not say which BSD licence.

pyinstaller.reason: Its metadata says GPLv2-or-later with an exception. Only the bootloader and loader (GPL-2.0-or-later with the Bootloader Exception) and the run-time hooks (Apache-2.0) are embedded in the frozen engine; see its COPYING.txt.

uvloop.expect: Permission is hereby granted, free of charge
uvloop.reason: Linux builds only (uvicorn uses it there). Dual-licensed: its README says "uvloop is dual-licensed under MIT and Apache 2.0 licenses" and it ships LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE. Its metadata has only the two classifiers, which do not say that they are a choice.

numpy.license: BSD-3-Clause AND 0BSD AND MIT AND Zlib AND CC0-1.0 AND LGPL-2.1-or-later AND GPL-3.0-or-later WITH GCC-exception-3.1
numpy.reason: Only in an engine built with the FMU pack (LIGHTSIM_FREEZE_FMU_PACK=1, backend/lightsim-backend.spec; the desktop build sets it). Its metadata names only the licences of its own code, but its Linux wheels bundle libquadmath (LGPL-2.1-or-later) and libgfortran (GPL-3.0-or-later with the GCC Runtime Library Exception) in numpy.libs, as its LICENSE.txt says. The LGPL part is allowed as a separate, replaceable file, listed with its source (the owner, 20 October 2026: lgpl below). Its win_amd64 wheels, which the desktop build freezes, bundle no libquadmath: platforms.win32.

lgpl.name: libquadmath (GCC's quad-precision maths library)
lgpl.files: the libraries in numpy.libs that NumPy's LICENSE.txt names for it, unmodified

win32.license: BSD-3-Clause AND 0BSD AND MIT AND Zlib AND CC0-1.0 AND GPL-3.0-or-later WITH GCC-exception-3.1
win32.reason: The win_amd64 wheels bundle no libquadmath: numpy.libs holds the OpenBLAS DLL, with the GCC runtime (libgfortran, GPL-3.0-or-later with the GCC Runtime Library Exception) linked into it, as their LICENSE.txt says (numpy 2.4.6), and the MSVC runtime. No LGPL part.

lxml.license: BSD-3-Clause AND PSF-2.0 AND MIT AND Zlib AND LGPL-2.1-or-later
lxml.reason: Only in an engine built with the FMU pack (LIGHTSIM_FREEZE_FMU_PACK=1, backend/lightsim-backend.spec; the desktop build sets it). Its metadata says BSD-3-Clause, but its binary wheels link in zlib, libxml2, libxslt and GNU libiconv, which its LICENSES.txt lists as LGPL 2.1 from lxml 6.1.3 on (the same file in every wheel; the Windows wheels link it in too, unnamed in 6.1.1: requirements-fmu.txt's floor). The LGPL part is allowed in lxml's own files, a separate, replaceable package, listed with its source (the owner, 20 October 2026: lgpl below).

lgpl.name: GNU libiconv
lgpl.files: lxml's compiled modules (lxml/etree and the others: .pyd on Windows, .so on Linux), which link it in, unmodified

setuptools.expect: Permission is hereby granted, free of charge
setuptools.reason: Its metadata names no licence; its LICENSE file is the MIT licence. PyInstaller pulls parts of it into the engine.
